title: 1 · Sounds and spelling
blurb: Read any Indonesian word aloud: the six vowels, the two e sounds, c, ng and ny, and how words end.

title: 2 · Greetings by time of day
blurb: Greet anyone at the right time of day with the right title, say thank you, excuse me and goodbye, and give your name.

title: 3 · Pronouns and titles: saya, kamu, Anda, Bapak, Ibu
blurb: Say I, you, he, she, we and they, and choose the polite way to say you: a title, a name, kamu or Anda.

title: 4 · Introducing yourself
blurb: Tell people your name, where you're from, where you live, your age, your job and how much Indonesian you speak, and ask them back.

title: 5 · A is B, with no 'to be'
blurb: Say what you are, how you feel and where you are with no word for am, is or are, and know the one place adalah belongs.

title: 6 · ini, itu: this and that
blurb: Point at things and talk about them: this is…, this book, that one, the one you want.

title: 7 · Noun + adjective: rumah besar
blurb: Describe things in Indonesian order, noun first: a big house, a plane ticket, very hot coffee.

title: 8 · Possession: buku saya, bukuku, bukunya
blurb: Say my, your, his, Budi's and my friend's the Indonesian way, with the owner after the thing, and say what you have with punya.

title: 9 · apa, siapa, di mana, kapan, berapa
blurb: Ask yes / no questions and use the question words: what, who, where, when, how much, how and why.

title: 10 · tidak and bukan
blurb: Say "not" the Indonesian way: tidak before verbs and describing words, bukan before nouns.

title: 11 · Numbers and prices
blurb: Count to a million, read prices in rupiah, and put numbers in the right place in a sentence.

title: 12 · Telling the time: jam, pukul, setengah
blurb: Ask and tell the time, say half past and quarter to, and name the days and dates.

title: 13 · ada: there is, have
blurb: Ask whether something is there, say there isn't any, and ask a shop or hotel what they have.

title: 14 · di, ke, dari
blurb: Say where you are, where you're going and where you're from, and place things on, under and next to each other.

title: 15 · Family and personal details
blurb: Talk about your family, tell older and younger siblings apart, and answer the questions Indonesians ask about it.

title: 16 · sudah, sedang, akan, belum
blurb: Say what is done, happening now, coming up or not done yet, without ever changing the verb.

title: 17 · The ber- prefix
blurb: Recognize and use the everyday ber- verbs for working, studying, swimming, playing and talking.

title: 18 · The me- prefix
blurb: Build the me- verbs for reading, writing, cooking, looking for and sending, with the right spelling.

title: 19 · mau, bisa, harus, boleh
blurb: Say what you want, can, must, may and need to do, with the helping word straight before the verb.

title: 20 · Asking and telling: tolong, minta, silakan, jangan
blurb: Order food, ask for things and favors politely, invite people in, and say 'don't'.

title: 21 · yang: which, who
blurb: Describe people and things with a whole phrase, and point out 'the red one' or 'the big one'.

title: 22 · The di- passive
blurb: Say what is done or was done to something, the way Indonesians do it every day: Kamarnya sudah dipesan.

title: 23 · lebih, paling: comparing
blurb: Compare prices and things: cheaper, the cheapest, the same size, too expensive.

title: 24 · Directions: junctions and places
blurb: Ask the way politely and follow the answer: left, right, straight on, the intersection, across from.

title: 25 · Daily activities and shopping
blurb: Talk through your day from getting up to going to bed, and buy things at a warung or market.

title: 26 · Plurals by repeating: buku-buku
blurb: Know when Indonesian marks 'more than one', when to repeat a word, and when never to.

title: 27 · Everyday spoken Indonesian
blurb: Understand the casual Indonesian you hear every day, and know when to use it and when not to.
